thesis: When Allah is forgotten, hypocrisy stops being a private defect and becomes a whole inverted social order — commanding wrong, forbidding right, closing the hand — which then re-enacts the same self-indulgent trajectory that destroyed stronger nations before it.

flags.quote: This mirrors the later description of believing men and women. Hypocrisy is not only individual inconsistency. It can become mutual reinforcement, shared atmosphere, and collective identity.
flags.issue: ADAB / KNOWN RISK. The file defines nifaq PURELY BEHAVIOURALLY throughout — inversion, closed hands, corrupted speech, forgetting Allah — and never once carries the definition that all four fetched editions open with, that nifaq is CONCEALED kufr behind a professed iman and therefore an interior state. al-Tabari 9:67: 'وهم الذين يظهرون للمؤمنين الإيمان بألسنتهم، ويسرون الكفر بالله ورسوله'; al-Muyassar: 'صنف واحد في إعلانهم الإيمان واستبطانهم الكفر'; al-Tabari on 9:97 adds that only Allah knows them ('والمنافق من خلقه... لا يخفى عليه منهم أحد'). Stripping the concealment element leaves a purely observable trait-list, which is exactly what makes this cluster usable as a checklist for calling other Muslims hypocrites. Mitigating: every application in the file is self-directed ('where in my own environment...', 'In what ways has forgetfulness of Allah begun to distort MY speech'), and the file never invites the reader to label anyone. But the guard is absent, on the single most sectarian-adversarial cluster in the surah.

flags.quote: The pattern is not only material enjoyment. It is indulgent immersion, especially in corrupt talk and heedless social atmosphere.
flags.issue: Softens khawd. All four editions tie 'وخضتم كالذي خاضوا' to lying and falsehood ABOUT ALLAH, not to loose social talk: al-Tabari 'وخضتم في الكذب والباطل على الله'; Ibn Kathir 'indulged in lies and falsehood'; al-Tabari expressly reads the whole ayah as the answer to 9:65 ('إنما كنا نخوض ونلعب' — mockery of Allah, His verses and His Messenger). The file's translation line likewise renders it 'the same idle talk'. Not false, but it moves a charge of mocking revelation into the register of a 'heedless social atmosphere'.

notes: Thesis is grounded: al-Tabari on 9:70 reads the historical list precisely as a warning that the munafiqun may be dealt with as the earlier nations were, and Ibn Kathir carries the Abu Hurayrah hadith ('you will follow the ways of those before you') applied to this very ayah, which licenses the file's universalizing move. Historical parallels (Nuh, 'Ad, Thamud, Ibrahim's people, Madyan, al-mu'tafikat) are listed bare with NO narrative detail — zero isra'iliyyat, clean. 'nasu Allaha fa-nasiyahum' is glossed acceptably ('leaves them abandoned to the consequences'), matching al-Tabari's 'تركهم الله من توفيقه وهدايته ورحمته' and al-Jalalayn's 'تركهم من لطفه'. This file carries NO tafsir attributions at all, so there is nothing to mis-attribute; it also carries no countable claims. FIXES: (1) add one paragraph, before or inside the 'ba'duhum min ba'd' anchor, carrying the four editions' definition of nifaq as concealed kufr known to Allah, with an explicit line that the passage is a mirror for the self and not a test to apply to other Muslims; (2) restore khawd to the commentators' 'lies and falsehood against Allah' / mockery of revelation. SEPARATE OBSERVATION for the human, not a rubric failure: this file is a v1 'codex-tadabbur' stub — 1,974 words, only 2 themes, no Architecture section, no One-Sentence Distillation, no Du'a — while the other three At-Tawbah files in this batch are 4,400-4,700-word v2 files. It is a rebuild candidate, not just a patch candidate.

thesis: Environment (distance from the Prophetic teaching centre) genuinely intensifies exposure to kufr, nifaq and ignorance of revealed limits, but it does not determine the heart — the same desert yields one man who reads spending as maghram and waits for the believers' collapse, and another who reads it as qurbah and is admitted into mercy.
notes: CRITICAL CHECK PASSES, and passes strongly. The file does not merely mention 9:99's counterbalance — the refusal to flatten IS its thesis. The introduction turns on it ('twice, it splits the category open: wa mina al-a'rabi'), Theme 1 is titled 'Harsh Environments Explain Pressure, Not Final Character', Theme 3 rests on the two mirrored subtypes, and the Architecture section names the pattern 'qualified generality broken by mirrored division'. It explicitly denies that ajdaru means 'every individual among them necessarily lacks knowledge' and warns readers off both uses of the verse ('Some people use environment as a weapon of condemnation... Others use it as an excuse of resignation. The Qur'an allows neither'). This is grounded in the fetched text: Ibn Kathir opens 9:97 by saying there are disbelievers, hypocrites AND believers among the bedouins, and al-Tabari 9:99 transmits Ibn Jurayj reading it as an express exception ('ثم استثنى فقال: ومن الأعراب من يؤمن'). VERIFIED ATTRIBUTIONS, each edition checked individually — no 'all four' claims appear anywhere in this file, only paired claims, and both pairs hold: 'Al-Tabari and al-Muyassar both emphasize that point' (al-Tabari: 'لجفائهم، وقسوة قلوبهم، وقلة مشاهدتهم لأهل الخير'; al-Muyassar: 'لجفائهم وقسوة قلوبهم وبعدهم عن العلم والعلماء ومجالس الوعظ والذكر') and 'Al-Tabari and Ibn Kathir both sharpen this beautifully' on maghram/qurubat (al-Tabari 9:98: 'غرما لزمه، لا يرجو له ثوابا، ولا يدفع به عن نفسه عقابا'; al-Tabari 9:99: 'ويبتغي بنفقة ما ينفق، مع طلب قربته من الله، دعاء الرسول واستغفاره له'; Ibn Kathir: 'as a fine, as a loss and a burden' / 'as way of achieving nearness to Allah and seeking the Messenger's invocation'). VERIFIED MECHANICALLY: 'wa mina al-a'rabi' appears exactly twice in the Qur'an, 9:98 and 9:99, so 'Immediately, twice' is correct (checked against quran-verses.json after stripping harakat and waqf marks and folding alif variants). Cross-references 2:261 (multiplication), 34:39 (yukhlifuhu / replacement), 63:7 (hypocrites telling people not to spend on those with the Messenger) all verify. Roots h-d-d, gh-r-m, q-r-b, r-b-s, d-w-r all match the corpus morphology. NON-BLOCKING ENRICHMENT NOTE for the human: the file never reports the commentators' identifications of specific groups — al-Jalalayn restricts 9:98's resentful spenders to Banu Asad and Ghatafan and 9:99's believers to Juhaynah and Muzaynah, and al-Tabari transmits Mujahid and 'Abd al-Rahman b. Ma'qil that 9:99 came down about Banu Muqarrin of Muzaynah. Those names are the strongest available anti-slur material, since they show the commentators reading BOTH halves as about identifiable groups rather than a people as such. Adding them would harden the file against exactly the adversarial quotation it already handles well by argument.

thesis: Sacred appearance does not sanctify corrupt intention: a structure founded on dirar, kufr, tafriq and irsad may stand before people for a time while already standing on the lip of its own collapse, and it goes on living inside its builders as ribah in the heart.

flags.quote: The commentators keep the image concrete rather than allegorical: Ibn Kathir speaks of the edge of a steep hole, and al-Muyassar of the rim of a pit already giving way toward collapse.
flags.issue: BREADTH-OF-ATTRIBUTION FAILURE, and in the direction of the dissent — the exact 006-al-anam pattern the rubric names. Two editions are named; the two unnamed ones both read the image EXPRESSLY as a parable. al-Tabari 9:109 interrupts his own commentary to say so: 'قال أبو جعفر: وإنما هذا مثل. يقول تعالى ذكره: أي هذين الفريقين خير؟ وأي هذين البناءين أثبت؟' — 'this is only a parable', and he then reads shafa jurufin harin as a simile for the man who began on nifaq and misguidance. al-Jalalayn is even more explicit: 'تمثيل للبناء على ضد التقوى بما يؤول إليه... وهو مثال مسجد قباء والثاني مثال مسجد الضرار'. So the summary sentence asserts that 'the commentators' keep the image concrete when half of them, unnamed, call it a mathal/tamthil. Fix: enumerate — Ibn Kathir and al-Muyassar hold the image concrete; al-Tabari and al-Jalalayn read it as a similitude — and note that the disagreement is itself useful, because the file's own move (from physical collapse to interior ribah) is closer to al-Tabari's than to the concrete reading it claims.

flags.quote: Discernment means we do not ask only whether something looks sacred. We ask whether it heals or divides, whether it grows purification or nourishes rivalry, whether it deepens taqwa or merely amplifies structure, whether those inside it love to purify themselves or only love to defend themselves.
flags.issue: AHKAM ADAB — missing the tadabbur-vs-fatwa line on the passage's most adversarially usable point. The passage is ahkam-bearing (the Prophet is forbidden to stand in the structure; al-Tabari transmits the order to Malik b. al-Dukhshum and Ma'n b. 'Adi, 'انطلقا إلى هذا المسجد الظالم أهله فاهدماه وحرقاه', al-Muyassar closes 'وقد هدم المسجد وأحرق', and al-Tabari 17200 already shows the fiqh afterlife in Shaqiq refusing to pray in a mosque he judged built 'على ضرار'). The file hands the reader a working test for evaluating religious institutions — and generalizes it explicitly to 'Religious spaces, initiatives, committees, platforms, media projects' — without ever saying that declaring an actual masjid a masjid dirar is a juristic determination, not a reading a tadabbur reader is licensed to make. That is precisely the sectarian misuse vector for 9:107-110. Mitigating and substantial: the file never names a real mosque or community, it repeatedly turns the test inward ('The self is fully capable of building Masjid al-Dirar on a smaller scale'; 'we all instinctively trust sacred form too much when our own ego is the builder'), and it pre-empts the obvious abuse ('This should not make us cynical... The Qur'an is not teaching suspicion as a worldview'). What is missing is one explicit boundary sentence, not the whole disposition.

notes: This is by a wide margin the most heavily and most precisely attributed file in the batch, and everything else in it checks out verbatim against the fetched editions. Verified individually: Ibn Kathir on Abu 'Amir al-Rahib — 'the Monk', of al-Khazraj, embraced Christianity before Islam and read the Scriptures, a known worshipper in the Jahiliyyah (all four details exact). al-Tabari 'وهم، فيما ذكر، اثنا عشر نفسا من الأنصار' — twelve men of the Ansar, and the file correctly flags 'فيما ذكر' as his own hedge. al-Muyassar's 'ليكون مكانا للكيد للمسلمين' (kayd), his 'انتظارا' for irsad, his Quba' division logic, and his closing 'وقد هدم المسجد وأحرق' — all four exact. al-Muyassar's oath detail is quoted almost word for word ('إلا الخير والرفق بالمسلمين، والتوسعة على الضعفاء العاجزين عن السير إلى مسجد قباء'), and the file's observation that the Qur'an preserved an ACCESSIBILITY argument rather than a crude one is a real and defensible reading of that text. al-Tabari's lam of oath is confirmed: 'ثم أقسم جل ثناؤه فقال: لمسجد أسس على التقوى'. His asas/asl gloss and 'من أول يوم ابتدئ في بنائه' are exact. al-Muyassar's two-register purification (water from najasat, plus wara' and istighfar) is exact, as is his a-fortiori note that the Prophet's own mosque is 'بطريق الأولى والأحرى'. The qira'at claim is exact and correctly placed: al-Tabari does open 9:109 with 'اختلفت القرأة', some readers of Madinah read both verbs passive, and he judges the two 'قراءتان متفقتا المعنى' — so 'nothing doctrinal turns on it' is his own verdict. On 9:110, al-Tabari's 'شكا ونفاقا في قلوبهم، يحسبون أنهم كانوا في بنائه محسنين' is reproduced exactly, including the easily-missed self-congratulation clause the file rightly calls the horror of the verse; his narrow exception 'إلا أن تتصدع قلوبهم فيموتوا' and al-Muyassar's wider one ('بقتلهم أو موتهم، أو بندمهم غاية الندم، وتوبتهم إلى ربهم، وخوفهم منه غاية الخوف') are both exact, and the file reports the disagreement as a disagreement rather than resolving it. One minor under-report, not flagged: on that exception the file names only al-Tabari (narrow) and al-Muyassar (wide), when Ibn Kathir ('until they die', on the authority of Ibn 'Abbas, Mujahid, Qatadah, Zayd b. Aslam, al-Suddi and others) and al-Jalalayn ('بأن يموتوا') both also hold the narrow reading — so al-Muyassar is the lone dissenter three-to-one, which strengthens rather than weakens the file's point but should be said. The file also handles al-Tabari's other ikhtilaf — whether 'the mosque founded on taqwa' is Quba' or the Prophet's mosque — honestly ('The point for tadabbur is the same either way'). No truncation artifacts. FIXES: enumerate the mathal dissent in the shafa juruf anchor, and add one explicit boundary sentence stating that this passage does not license a reader to judge an existing mosque or community a masjid dirar.

thesis: Allah does not judge by outward non-participation: He clears the weak, the sick and the poor whose sincerity held, honours the tears of those who sought a way and were refused, and narrows blame precisely onto the wealthy who wanted incapacity's innocence without incapacity's cost.

flags.quote: The outer frame is verse 90 and verse 93: at the beginning, excuse-makers and liars are named; at the end, blame is explicitly restricted to those who sought permission while rich.
flags.issue: AHKAM IKHTILAF — a contested reading of al-mu'adhdhirun (9:90) is built into the file's structural thesis with no acknowledgement that it is contested, and it is the MINORITY reading of the four fetched editions. The file's ring architecture requires verse 90's first group to sit in the accusation frame. Three of the four editions read them instead as genuinely excused. Ibn Kathir: 'Ad-Dahhak said that Ibn 'Abbas said that they were those who had valid excuses.' al-Jalalayn: 'المعتذرون بمعنى المعذورين وقرئ به... ليؤذن لهم في القعود لعذرهم فأذن لهم' — i.e. the Prophet granted them leave BECAUSE their excuse was real. al-Muyassar: 'يعتذرون إلى رسول الله ﷺ، ويبينون له ما هم فيه من الضعف وعدم القدرة على الخروج للغزو'. Only al-Tabari argues for the reading the file assumes, and even he stages the dispute at length — he reports Ibn 'Abbas and Mujahid reciting المعْذِرون lightened and glossing 'هم أهل العذر', against Qatadah ('اعتذروا بالكذب') and Mujahid's other narration about a group of Banu Ghifar 'فلم يعذرهم الله' — before settling on the doubled reading. This is exactly a settled ruling presented without its ikhtilaf, on an excuse-from-jihad passage. Fix: report the two readings of al-mu'adhdhirun in the Architecture section (and soften the frontmatter translation 'the excuse-makers'), and note that on the majority reading verse 90's first clause is itself part of the absolution, which does not destroy the ring — 'those who lied to Allah and His Messenger' still holds the outer frame — but does change who is standing in it.

flags.quote: Al-Tabari explains this sincerity in terms of truthful religion and non-betrayal in their remaining behind.
flags.issue: MISATTRIBUTION. al-Tabari does not gloss nasahu in those terms at all. His whole comment on the clause is a restatement — 'ليس عليهم إثم، إذا نصحوا لله ولرسوله في مغيبهم عن الجهاد مع رسول الله ﷺ' and 'ليس على من أحسن فنصح لله ولرسوله في تخلفه... لعذر يعذر به، طريق يتطرق عليه فيعاقب من قبله'. Neither 'truthful religion' nor 'non-betrayal' appears. The content the file assigns to him belongs to the two editions it does not name here: al-Muyassar has the religion element ('إذا أخلصوا لله ورسوله، وعملوا بشرعه') and al-Jalalayn has the non-betrayal element and is specific about it ('في حال قعودهم بعدم الإرجاف والتثبيط والطاعة' — no rumour-mongering, no discouraging others, and obedience). Fix: reassign — al-Muyassar for sincerity-plus-shari'a, al-Jalalayn for the concrete non-betrayal conditions, and let al-Tabari carry what he actually adds, that the clearance is 'لعذر يعذر به', tied to a genuine excuse.

notes: The central thesis and the One-Sentence Distillation survive both flags intact and are well grounded — Ibn Kathir organises 9:91-92 exactly as the file does ('Legitimate Excuses for staying away from Jihad', permanent impediments then temporary ones), and carries the Anas hadith 'إن بالمدينة أقواما ما قطعتم واديا ولا سرتم سيرا إلا وهم معكم... نعم حبسهم العذر', which is the strongest possible support for the file's Theme 2 (tears and blocked longing as real participation). VERIFIED: 'Al-Tabari and Ibn Kathir both preserve the basic frame: they turned back not with relief, but with tears' — al-Tabari 17079 from Ibn 'Abbas, 'فتولوا ولهم بكاء، وعزيز عليهم أن يجلسوا عن الجهاد', and Ibn Kathir via Mujahid on Banu Muqarrin of Muzaynah. 'Ibn Kathir reads it through real excuse joined to loyal concern' — confirmed ('providing that when they remain behind, they do not spread malice or try to discourage Muslims from fighting'), and the file correctly carries that condition forward into its own prose ('not to lie, not to sabotage, not to harden'). ALL EIGHT cross-references verify against quran-verses.json: 2:286 (no soul burdened beyond capacity), 48:17 (blame lifted from the blind, the lame, the sick), 4:95 (qa'idun not equal to mujahidun, 'ghayr uli al-darar' — and the file's handling of it, 'distinction is not the same as contempt', is careful and correct), 9:46 ('لو أرادوا الخروج لأعدوا له عدة'), 9:81 ('فرح المخلفون بمقعدهم'), 9:44, 9:45, 9:86 ('استأذنك أولو الطول منهم'). Roots n-s-h and f-y-d match the corpus morphology; the innama restriction reading is standard and al-Muyassar confirms the target ('إنما الإثم واللوم على الأغنياء... وهم المنافقون الأغنياء'). NO countable or 'all four' claims appear in this file. Two minor items not flagged: (1) the structural claim that 'Most groups are spoken about in the third person, but the middle scene suddenly becomes intimate' is slightly loose — 9:93 also carries direct address in 'يستأذنونك' — though the file's actual point, that 9:92 is the only two-turn exchange with the Prophet, holds; (2) the file renders al-khawalif as 'those who stay behind' and never reports the standard gloss preserved by Ibn Kathir and al-Muyassar that it means the women and the excused who remained at home ('مع النساء وأهل الأعذار'), which would sharpen its own point about the rich choosing the rear place. No truncation artifacts.
